title: A Autopsy for the Portrait Revisited
premise: Edmund Iversen, the unassuming coroner of Grayhaven Bay, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, keeping his gift for reading bodies a secret. When a drowned woman washes up wearing clothes stolen from his own closet, he realizes someone is staging murders to frame him—and that person has studied his old case files with unsettling intimacy. As Edmund races to decode the killer's pattern, which mirrors the three deaths he once solved in secret, he falls for Mara Voss, the witness whose testimony could either save him or condemn him. In the end, Edmund must expose himself publicly to trap the killer at the tide flats where it all began, choosing justice over invisibility and love over duty to the dead.
about_author: Odile Sandoval is the pen name of a former forensic technician who left coastal pathology work after a decade of writing case notes no one read. She now lives above a bookbindery, where she repairs damaged spines and writes novels about people who speak for the dead.

chapters.title: The Man Who Names Graves
chapters.summary: Edmund Iversen's POV. A quiet morning in the Grayhaven morgue establishes Edmund's ritual: he speaks each name aloud before autopsy, a habit born from the three deaths he secretly solved. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—he is competent, invisible, and content to remain so.

chapters.title: Salt and Wool
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A body washes up at Miller's Tide Flats wearing Edmund's own gray cardigan and scarf, items stolen from his closet. Police find his spare house key nearby. Panic beneath clinical calm; the beat is the shattering of his safe anonymity.

chapters.title: Witness at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Mara, who found the body while sketching the flats, describes a figure watching her from the dunes—wearing what looked like Edmund's coat. She hesitates to name him, sensing something wrong. Beat: reluctant attraction to a man she may have doomed.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He reviews his private notes on the three deaths he quietly corrected—a fall, a fire, a drowning—and realizes the new victim's wounds replicate the drowning case exactly. Someone knows his methods. Beat: cold dread of being known.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor Arrives
chapters.summary: Detective Adaeze Okafor's POV. A sharp outsider detective is assigned, suspicious of both Edmund and the too-convenient evidence. She interviews him with surgical courtesy. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins; Edmund feels seen for the first time and hates it.

chapters.title: The Closet Key
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He traces how someone entered his home—no forced entry, only the spare key kept in a hollowed hymnal. Only four people ever knew its location. Beat: paranoia tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Sketches of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara shows Edmund her sketches from the morning of the discovery; one contains a partial face she didn't realize she'd drawn. They meet properly for the first time, guarded but drawn together. Beat: fragile alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He exhumes records from the second staged death—the fire—and finds the widow still living in town, terrified into silence years ago. She whispers a name half-heard: 'the one who reads.' Beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor presents Edmund with evidence timeline discrepancies and asks why an ordinary coroner keeps such meticulous unofficial files. Edmund deflects, barely. Beat: the cost of secrets surfacing under pressure.

chapters.title: A Second Body, Dressed for Him
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A second victim appears, this time wearing Edmund's late father's watch—something never catalogued publicly. The killer isn't just framing him; they're performing his biography back at him. Beat: horror deepening into intimacy.

chapters.title: Mara Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pressured by police, Mara gives a statement describing the watcher, nearly confirming their identity as Edmund. That night she confesses her doubt to him on the seawall. Beat: love against duty crystallizing between them.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He discovers his confidential case files were copied—paper dust, misaligned folders—by someone with legitimate access. The list narrows to courthouse staff and one retired clerk, Silas Renner. Beat: the hunter realizing he was always the quarry.

chapters.title: Silas Renner's Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor investigates Renner, finding he lost his daughter in a death Edmund privately reclassified years ago—reclassified away from the man Renner believed guilty. Motive emerges: not revenge on Edmund, but a twisted demand that he solve one more death, publicly. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts his own guilt: his secret corrections saved some and abandoned others, including Renner's daughter's unresolved case. He tells Mara everything. Beat: humility; the hero discovering his own complicity.

chapters.title: The Third Costume
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara receives a package containing a dress from the third unsolved case and a note: 'He knows. Ask him why he stayed quiet.' She realizes the killer is orchestrating witnesses, not just victims. Beat: terror weaponized through her.

chapters.title: Okafor's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor finds proof Edmund tampered with old reports—but also proof the tampering exposed real murderers. Duty says arrest; justice says listen. She chooses an uneasy partnership. Beat: justice outside the law taking institutional form.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's File
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Decoding the staged details, Edmund realizes Renner is building toward a final tableau at the tide flats on the spring equinox tide—the anniversary of his daughter's drowning. Beat: the trap inverting; Edmund decides to walk into it armed.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Edmund and Okafor stage a public announcement that the reclassification of Renner's daughter's case will be reopened, luring Renner to finish his tableau early. Mara insists on playing her role despite the risk. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the flats, Renner takes Mara hostage, demanding Edmund confess publicly to every life his silence cost. Edmund does—not as defeat but as testimony, naming the guilty aloud while Okafor closes in. Beat: climax; truth as weapon.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Renner, undone by hearing his daughter's name spoken with honor rather than pity, surrenders to the incoming tide; Edmund pulls him back, insisting he face trial. Beat: mercy chosen over vengeance; justice reclaimed within law.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Renner's trial forces every buried case into daylight; Edmund testifies fully, ending his career of shadows. Some colleagues turn away; others follow his lead. Beat: reckoning and quiet vindication.

chapters.title: A Name for Every Grave
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, months later. Edmund and Mara walk the flats at dawn; he has added Renner's daughter's name to his morning litany. No longer invisible, he finds visibility costs less than he feared when shared. Beat: resolution—love, accountability, peace.
